title: A release
summary: How a commit becomes the running release on a host. The top row happens before anything stops; the second row is the outage, guarded by a marker file; the third row is what serves and watches the result, and what happens when a gate fails. There is no automatic schema rollback.

boxes.label: Release workflow
boxes.detail: Runs the pull request checks and the release-tooling, adapter and Mosquitto checks, then builds eight images and pushes them to the container registry tagged with the commit: api, api-web, portal, admin, runtime, simulator, adapter-manager and adapter-runtime. The runtime image also holds broker-admin.

boxes.label: release.json
boxes.detail: The workflow records each pushed image as name@sha256 digest and assembles them, with the commit, into release.json. It is uploaded with deploy/release, deploy/ansible and tooling/release as the single-node-release artifact. A second dispatch can export the same images as an offline archive.

boxes.label: ship.py
boxes.detail: Verifies the staged source archive against its checksum and commit, validates with the new release's tooling, then takes the operation lock and checks the running release: no marker files, the expected commit, no demo data. It counts rows, and --preflight stops here. Otherwise it swaps in the new source and calls that release's own deploy. A first installation runs manage.py deploy directly.

boxes.label: Validate and render
boxes.detail: validate refuses an environment file that others can read, missing or non-generated secrets, and any image that is not an immutable digest. render writes the NATS, Prometheus, Alertmanager, database-role and extra Caddy files from the private environment. Deploy then requires MQTT certificates (manage.py certificates) and off-host backup access, pulls the images, and creates the broker's security file if there is none.

boxes.label: Checkpoint
boxes.detail: Taken with the release that is still running, not the new images. It stops ingress and the broker, waits 45 seconds for command deadlines, stops writers and NATS, then sends a database dump, the cold state directories, the environment and the manifest to an off-host Restic repository. What was running restarts even after an error. The old manifest is kept as previous-release.json.

boxes.label: Stop Caddy and writers
boxes.detail: Deploy writes the marker, then stops adapters, Caddy, simulators, the API, every worker, the scheduler and the runtime, so nothing writes during migrations and only one runtime ever runs. NATS and the broker are recreated to pick up rendered files, then broker-admin.

boxes.label: Migrations
boxes.detail: Two one-off jobs: Laravel's php artisan migrate --force for the public schema, then the runtime image with --migrate for device_runtime. After them come the additive PermissionSeeder and devices:reprovision-broker. The running runtime never migrates by itself in a release.

boxes.label: Recreate applications
boxes.detail: Every service without a profile except the database, NATS, the broker and broker-admin is recreated from the new images. The broker is left alone here because recreating it would drop every device a second time. Tenant adapter containers are started again.

boxes.label: Readiness and smoke
boxes.detail: Waits up to two minutes for api-web/health/ready inside the network, then requests the public app, admin and API hosts over HTTPS. Only when all answer 200 is the manifest written as current-release.json and the marker removed. ship.py then runs the release checks and compares its row counts.

boxes.label: Timers and monitoring
boxes.detail: The host playbook installs systemd timers that call manage.py: backup daily, certificates twice a day, metrics and monitoring_heartbeat every minute. They share the deploy's lock and wait for it. Prometheus, Alertmanager, Loki, Alloy and Grafana run in the same Compose project; the heartbeat is pinged only when every health check passes, because same-host monitoring cannot report a dead host.

boxes.label: Caddy
boxes.sub: TLS for app, admin, api, ops
boxes.detail: The only web entry point, on 80 and 443. It proxies app to the portal, admin to the admin app and api to api-web, and answers 404 for /internal and /api/internal paths. The ops host serves Grafana, Alertmanager and the runbook to the VPN range only; everyone else gets 403. MQTT does not pass through Caddy: the broker serves 8883 with its own certificate.

boxes.label: Deployment incomplete
boxes.detail: If anything fails after the marker is written, it stays. Further deploys and backups refuse to run until a person reconciles which images and which schema are actually in place and removes it.

boxes.label: Roll back or restore
boxes.detail: Rolling back is deploying previous-release.json, and only when the schema is still compatible. Otherwise manage.py restore puts a checkpoint onto an empty, isolated host and leaves it quarantined: only the database starts, and a RESTORE_QUARANTINE marker blocks deploys until a person has reviewed it.

steps.text: A v* tag runs the checks and builds eight images. Each pushed image's digest goes into release.json with the commit.
For an upgrade, the manifest and a source archive of the same commit are staged on the host. ship.py checks them, and with --preflight stops before changing anything.
ship.py installs the new source and runs its deploy. Deploy validates the private environment and the manifest, then renders configuration files.
With images pulled, the release that is still running takes a checkpoint to the off-host repository. If anything fails up to here, the old release is still running and ship.py puts its source back.
The DEPLOYMENT_INCOMPLETE marker is written, then Caddy, the API, the workers, the scheduler and the runtime stop.
With no writers, the Laravel migration job runs, then the runtime's own migration job, then permissions and broker credentials are re-applied.
The application services are recreated from the new digests. The broker is not recreated again, so devices reconnect once.
Caddy comes back with them and is again the only way in from the web, with internal paths answered 404.
Deploy waits for the API to report ready inside the network, then checks the public hosts over HTTPS.
When every gate passes, the manifest becomes current-release.json and the marker is removed. The timers' backups, metrics and heartbeats now use that manifest.
If a gate fails, the marker stays and blocks further deploys and backups.
A person reconciles the state: redeploy previous-release.json if the schema allows it, otherwise restore the checkpoint on an isolated host, in quarantine.
